I feel sore all the time. Any way to feel better without stopping? Do I just have to push through it?

Without being pedantic, it depends on what you mean by 'sore'. If the soreness is muscle/motion specific and shows up a day or two later, it is almost certainly Delayed-Onset Muscular Soreness (or DOMS), and the intensity and duration of DOMS will decrease with continued training, to the point where it may be largely imperceptible. Generally, one would work through such soreness, likely after extra warm-up and possibly with temporarily less intensity. If it's truly painful, it may be more serious (and possibly a reason to see a doctor). If the soreness you describe is more lethargy and feeling generally drained, and it has been continuing for some time (probably over 2 weeks), it sounds more like habitually insufficient recovery. Common reasons for that can be insufficient food, insufficient sleep, high stress, etc. In that case, you may want to shift things around to obtain a more workable balance for your lifestyle.

Your body will get used to it. Just make sure to eat a lot of food, especially protein so that you can recover faster and better. One of my biggest mistakes when I started to work out was not eating enough food and protein.

It will pass after a few days. It's just a sign that you've worked a muscle that isn't used to being worked.

The most important thing is to SLEEP. A lot of people overlook this and it's huge. Try to get at least 7 hours. Good luck.
If you want your soreness to go away, continue working out. If you workout, your muscles will be flooded with blood, which in turn, will help your muscles go through a faster recovery time.

Pain is indeed weakness leaving the body, but popping a few ibuprofen before a workout never hurt me. Drinking a gallon of water a day is a must when lifting. It makes a huge difference for your recovery.
It gave me the feeling of progress.
You can try icing your muscles and taking a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory. The soreness will last, at first it's almost unbearable but soon it'll be something you crave.

What does your workout schedule and routine look like (i.e. exercises, sets, repetitions)? Another commentor mentioned DOMS and this is most likely the issue, but being new to exercise and pushing your body too far too fast when it's unaccustomed to that level of work can lead to injury.

Damn, this reminds me of that night and next morning laying in my bed after my first workout. My advice: just keep working out. your body gets used to the additional stress and you wont notice it much as time progresses.

If you keep going consistently your body will adapt and you won't feel as sore. The first few days I worked out I could hardly move the next day, but after several months that doesn't happen to me much anymore.

Push through it! As time passes you will not get as sore, but if you get into it then you will look forward to the days where you are sore... Because then you know that you really pushed yourself and hit those weights hard. Mind over body!
